record.title: Topological amenability conjecture on connected components
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a topological group. Write ${G^*}^{00}_{\operatorname{top}}$ and ${G^*}^{000}_{\operatorname{top}}$ for the topological model-theoretic connected components of $G^*$.

**Topological amenability conjecture.** If $G$ is amenable, then

$$
{G^*}^{00}_{\operatorname{top}}={G^*}^{000}_{\operatorname{top}}.
$$

This is the topological analogue of the definable amenability conjecture. The source introduces it as a conjecture and develops a language with predicates for all open subsets to address it; no resolution status is stated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Krzysztof Krupinski and Anand Pillay, “Amenability, definable groups, and automorphism groups”, arXiv:1612.07560 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07560

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

record.title: Weak definable amenability conjecture for discrete definable groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a group definable in an arbitrary structure $M$. Write ${G^*}^{00}_M$ and ${G^*}^{000}_M$ for the model-theoretic connected components of $G^*$.

**Weak definable amenability conjecture.** If $G$ is weakly definably amenable, then

$$
{G^*}^{00}_M={G^*}^{000}_M.
$$

This is the discrete specialization of the generalized definable topological amenability conjecture. The supplied text presents it while discussing that specialization and gives no resolution status for it.
record.source_name: Krzysztof Krupinski and Anand Pillay, “Amenability, definable groups, and automorphism groups”, arXiv:1612.07560 (2019).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07560

record.title: Positive-rank twist conjecture for the elliptic curves associated with the quartic equation
record.statement:
Let $h$ be an arbitrary fixed rational number. For each rational number $t$, consider the elliptic curve

$$
E(h)_t: Y^2=Z^3-(3h^2t^8)Z-(h^4t^{16}+h^2t^8).
$$

**Positive-rank twist conjecture.** There exists at least one rational number $t$ such that the rank of $E(h)_t$ is positive.

The conjecture would complete the elliptic-curve method for producing infinitely many integer solutions of the quartic Diophantine equation $A^4+hB^4=C^4+hD^4$ for every rational $h$. The source reports that suitable values of $t$ were found for many $h$, but that the proof for arbitrary $h$ remains difficult.
record.source_name: Farzali Izadi and Mehdi Baghalagdam, “Is the quartic Diophantine equation A^4+hB^4=C^4+hD^4 solvable for any integer h?”, arXiv:1701.02602 (2017).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1009.5389](https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.5389).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.02602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

record.title: Asymptotic normality for fixed $d$
record.statement:
Let $X_{d,n}$ be the size of a uniformly random $(n,dn-1)$-core partition with distinct parts, with mean $\mu_{d,n}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_{d,n}$. Fix $d$ and let $n$ tend to infinity.

**Fixed-$d$ normality conjecture.** For fixed $d$, the distribution of $X_{d,n}$ is asymptotically normal. That is,

$$
\frac{X_{d,n}-\mu_{d,n}}{\sigma_{d,n}}
$$

approaches the standard normal distribution as $n\to\infty$.

The conjecture is motivated by the observed limiting standardized moments $0,1,0,3,0,15,\dots$. It is presented as an experimentally supported conjecture, with no proof or resolution stated.
record.source_name: Anthony Zaleski, “Explicit expressions for the moments of the size of an (n, dn-1)-core partition with distinct parts”, arXiv:1702.05634 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05634

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Petersen graph vertex-irreducibility conjecture
record.statement:
A bridgeless cubic class 2 graph $G$ is **vertex-irreducible** if, for any two vertices $x,y\in V(G)$, the graph $G-\{x,y\}$ cannot be extended to a bridgeless cubic class 2 graph by adding edges.

**Petersen graph vertex-irreducibility conjecture.** The Petersen graph is the only vertex-irreducible bridgeless cubic class 2 graph.

A vertex-irreducible cubic graph is known to be cyclically 5-edge-connected, and the conjecture was verified computationally for all cubic bridgeless graphs with at most 36 vertices. The general statement remains open in the source.
record.source_name: M. A. Fiol, G. Mazzuoccolo and E. Steffen, “On measures of edge-uncolorability of cubic graphs: A brief survey and some new results”, arXiv:1702.07156 (2017).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1504.03500](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03500), [arXiv:0901.0759](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.0759).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07156

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Chern's affine Bernstein conjecture
record.statement:
Let $u\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth and locally uniformly convex, and suppose its graph is an affine maximal graph, meaning that $u$ satisfies the affine maximal surface equation

$$
\sum_{i,j=1}^{2}\frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(U^{ij}w)=0,
\qquad w=[\det D^2u]^{-\frac{3}{4}},
$$

where $U=(U^{ij})$ is the cofactor matrix of $D^2u$. **Chern's conjecture.** The graph of $u$ must be an elliptic paraboloid. This is the two-dimensional affine Bernstein problem; it was proved by Trudinger and Wang in 2000, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Nam Q. Le, “The second boundary value problem of the prescribed affine mean curvature equation and related linearized Monge-Ampère equation”, arXiv:1702.08366 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08366

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Edrei's conjecture on weak local contractions
record.statement: Let $X$ be a compact metric space, and let $f:X\to X$ be a **weak local contraction**, meaning that for every $x\in X$ there exists an $r_x>0$ such that $d(x,y)<r_x$ implies $d(f(x),f(y))\leq d(x,y)$. A map $f$ is a **local isometry** if for every $x\in X$ there exists an $R_x>0$ such that $d(x,y)<R_x$ implies $d(f(x),f(y))=d(x,y)$. **Edrei's conjecture.** Every weak local contraction $f:X\to X$ on a compact metric space is a local isometry. Edrei's conjecture was disproved by Williams in 1954, who constructed four maps for which every point is a weak contraction point but some points are not isometry points.
record.source_name: Jan P. Boronski, Jiri Kupka and Piotr Oprocha, “Edrei's Conjecture revisited”, arXiv:1703.01816 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.01816

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Determinant formula for the weak-order raising operator
record.statement:
Let $W_n$ be the weak order on the symmetric group $S_n$, ranked by inversion number, and let $U$ be the order-raising operator defined by

$$
U(u)=\sum_{i\,:\,\ell(us_i)=1+\ell(u)}i\cdot us_i.
$$

For $0\leq k<\frac12\binom n2$, let $\tilde{D}(n,k)$ be the matrix of the map $U^{\binom n2-2k}\colon \mathbb{Q}(W_n)_k\to\mathbb{Q}(W_n)_{\binom n2-k}$ after dividing every entry by $(\binom n2-2k)!$. **The determinant conjecture.**

$$
\det \tilde{D}(n,k)=\pm\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(\frac{\binom n2-(k+i)}{k-i}\right)^{\#(W_n)_i}.
$$

This formula has been verified for all pairs $(n,k)$ with $n\leq 12$ and $k\leq 5$, as well as in a few additional cases. If true, it would establish the required nonsingularity of the raising maps and hence strong Sperner properties for the weak order.
record.source_name: Richard P. Stanley, “Some Schubert shenanigans”, arXiv:1704.00851 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00851

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).

record.title: Algebraicity conjecture for cluster generating functions of generalized consecutive patterns
record.statement: Let $m\geq4$ and let $\tau=134\ldots(m-1)2m$ be the consecutive pattern of length $m$. Let $T(x)$ be the cluster generating function specified by the preceding conjectural hypergeometric formula. **Algebraicity conjecture.** The solution $T(x)$ is algebraic, being the root of a polynomial of degree $m-2$. This conjecture extends the explicitly verified algebraic cases and predicts a uniform algebraic description for the cluster generating functions associated with this family of consecutive patterns; its validity for arbitrary $m\geq4$ remains open.
record.source_name: Nicholas R Beaton, Andrew R Conway and Anthony J Guttmann, “On consecutive pattern-avoiding permutations of length 4, 5 and beyond”, arXiv:1704.08839 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08839

record.title: Equality of two quadrant marked mesh pattern polynomials
record.statement:
Let $Q_{132}^{(a,b,\tau,c)}(t,x)$ denote the polynomial associated with 132-avoiding permutations and the indicated quadrant marked mesh pattern parameters. The parameters are $(0,k,\emptyset,0)$ and $(1,k-1,\emptyset,0)$, with $k\geq 1$.

**Equality conjecture.** For all $k\geq 1$, we have

$$
Q_{132}^{(0,k,\emptyset,0)}(t,x)=Q_{132}^{(1,k-1,\emptyset,0)}(t,x).
$$

The equality is motivated by the observed coincidence of the corresponding polynomials. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Dun Qiu and Jeffrey B. Remmel, “Quadrant marked mesh patterns in 123-avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1705.00164 (2018).

record.title: Artin-group conjecture for complements of hypocycloids
record.statement:
A hypocycloid is determined by coprime integers $0<\ell<k$; set $N:=k+\ell$, and let $\mathcal{C}_{k,\ell}$ denote its complexified plane algebraic curve. The **Artin-group conjecture.** For any such pair, the fundamental group of the complement of $\mathcal{C}_{k,\ell}$ is the Artin group of the $N$-gon.

This conjecture predicts a uniform combinatorial description of the fundamental groups of complements of complexified hypocycloids. It is supported by partial results and computations for all hypocycloids with $N\leq 11$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Enrique Artal Bartolo, José Ignacio Cogolludo-Agustín and Jorge Martín-Morales, “Wirtinger curves, Artin groups, and hypocycloids”, arXiv:1705.03268 (2017).

record.title: Conjecture on arbitrarily long sequences of consecutive happy numbers in even negative bases
record.statement:
Let $b\leq -12$ be even. A positive integer is **$b$-happy** if iterating the sum-of-squares-of-digits map in base $b$ eventually reaches $1$. A finite sequence of consecutive positive integers is a sequence of consecutive $b$-happy numbers.

**Conjecture.** For every even integer $b\leq -12$, there exist arbitrarily long finite sequences of consecutive $b$-happy numbers.

This extends the preceding theorem for the smaller even negative bases and the result for odd negative bases, leaving the even bases $b\leq -12$ as the remaining case addressed here.
record.source_name: Helen G. Grundman and Pamela E. Harris, “Sequences of Consecutive Happy Numbers in Negative Bases”, arXiv:1705.04648 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04648

record.title: Dujella's conjecture on Diophantine quadruples
record.statement:
Let $S=\{-4,-3,-1,3,5,8,12,20\}$. A **$D(n)$-quadruple** of natural numbers is a set of four distinct natural numbers such that the product of any two distinct elements increased by $n$ is a square of an integer.

**Dujella's conjecture.** For every $n\in S$, there does not exist a $D(n)$-quadruple of natural numbers.

For most integers outside the exceptional set $S$, existence results are known, while the cases in $S$ remain unanswered. The conjecture concerns the unresolved exceptional values of the parameter $n$.
record.source_name: Alan Filipin and Ana Jurasić, “A polynomial variant of a problem of Diophantus and its consequences”, arXiv:1705.09194 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.09194

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

record.title: Füredi's equi-sized chain partition conjecture for the Boolean lattice
record.statement:
Let $2^{[n]}$ denote the Boolean lattice of subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let a **chain** be a subset whose elements are pairwise comparable by inclusion. For a positive integer $n$, set

$$
l=\left\lfloor\frac{2^n}{\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Füredi's conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, the Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}$ can be partitioned into $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ chains such that the size of each chain is $l$ or $l+1$.

If true, this would give a partition into chains of size $(\sqrt{\pi/2}+o(1))\sqrt n$. The conjecture remains open; a weaker result gives a partition into the same number of chains whose sizes lie between $0.8\sqrt n$ and $25\sqrt n$.
record.source_name: István Tomon, “Forbidden induced subposets in the grid”, arXiv:1705.09551 (2017).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1509.07346](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.07346).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.09551

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2017). “While Conjecture is still open, the author of this paper proved that $2^{[n]}$ can be partitioned into $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ chains such that the size of each chain in the partition is between $0.8\sqrt{n}$ and $25\sqrt{n}$.”

record.title: Tightened Goldbach conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the natural numbers and $\mathbb{P}$ the primes. For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq 6$, let $k_n$ be the index of the uniquely determined prime $p_{k_n}\in\mathbb{P}$ satisfying

$$
p_{k_n}^2+p_{k_n}\leq 2\cdot n<p_{k_n+1}^2+p_{k_n+1}.
$$

**Tightened Goldbach conjecture.** For all $n\geq 6$, there exist primes $q_1,q_2\in\mathbb{P}$ such that

$$
p_{k_n}<q_1<p_{k_n}^2,\qquad q_1+q_2=2\cdot n.
$$

The source reports verification for all $n$ with $12\leq 2\cdot n\leq 10^8$, but gives no proof for the remaining cases.
record.source_name: Mario Ziller and John F. Morack, “Divisibility in paired progressions, Goldbach's conjecture, and the infinitude of prime pairs”, arXiv:1706.00317 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00317

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

record.title: The des-Wilf equivalences among four-letter non-classical patterns
record.statement:
For a permutation pattern $\tau$, let $F_n^{\operatorname{des}}(\tau;q)$ denote the descent generating polynomial over permutations in $\operatorname{Av}_n(\tau)$, and write $\tau\equiv_{\operatorname{des}}\rho$ when $F_n^{\operatorname{des}}(\tau;q)=F_n^{\operatorname{des}}(\rho;q)$ for every $n$. **The des-Wilf equivalences conjecture.** The following equivalences hold:

$$
1243\equiv_{\operatorname{des}}3412\qquad\text{and}\qquad 1342\equiv_{\operatorname{des}}2413.
$$

These conjectured equalities concern descent-preserving enumeration of permutations avoiding the displayed non-classical patterns; the paper reports supporting data but no closed forms for the relevant generating polynomials are known.
record.source_name: Caden Bielawa, Robert Davis, Daniel Greeson and Qinhan Zhou, “Descents and des-Wilf Equivalence of Permutations Avoiding Certain Non-Classical Patterns”, arXiv:1706.06231 (2018).
record.references:

record.title: Restricted size Ramsey number conjecture for paths versus cycles
record.statement:
Let $P_3$ be the path on three vertices and let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices. Write $r^{*}(P_3,C_n)$ for the restricted size Ramsey number of $P_3$ versus $C_n$. **Restricted size Ramsey number conjecture.** For all $n\geq 10$,

$$
r^{*}(P_{3},C_{n})=2n-2.
$$

The paper establishes six values for $7\leq n\leq 12$ and gives an upper bound for even $n\geq 10$; the conjecture concerns the remaining general equality and is presented as an open direction for further investigation.
record.source_name: Joanna Cyman and Tomasz Dzido, “Restricted size Ramsey number for P_3 versus cycles”, arXiv:1706.08134 (2018).

record.title: Distinct cubic fields conjecture for the initial point sets $I_{0,c}$
record.statement:
Let $I_{0,c}$ be the initial point set associated with the positive integer $c$, whose elements are cubic algebraic integers. **Distinct cubic fields conjecture.** For every $c\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and all distinct $\alpha,\beta\in I_{0,c}$, one has

$$
\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)\neq\mathbb{Q}(\beta).
$$

Equivalently, each element of $I_{0,c}$ belongs to a different cubic number field. The claim is supported by the authors' computational experiments for $1\leq c\leq 5\times 10^4$, but no proof or resolution is given.
record.source_name: Asaki Saito and Akihiro Yamaguchi, “Pseudorandom number generator based on the Bernoulli map on cubic algebraic integers”, arXiv:1706.08472 (2017).
record.references:

record.title: The Main Conjecture for Vinogradov mean values
record.statement:
For integers $s,k\geq 1$, let $J_{s,k}(X)$ count the integral solutions with $1\leq x_i\leq X$ to

$$
x_1^j+\cdots+x_s^j=x_{s+1}^j+\cdots+x_{2s}^j,\qquad 1\leq j\leq k.
$$

**The Main Conjecture.** For all integers $s,k\geq 1$,

$$
J_{s,k}(X)\ll_{s,k,\epsilon}X^\epsilon\left(X^s+X^{2s-\frac12k(k+1)}\right),
$$

for all $X\geq 1$ and every $\epsilon>0$. The two terms correspond respectively to diagonal solutions and the contribution from solutions concentrated near the origin in frequency space. The conjecture was resolved in full in 2015 by Bourgain, Demeter, and Guth, following Wooley's major advances and earlier resolution of the first nontrivial case.
record.source_name: Lillian B. Pierce, “The Vinogradov Mean Value Theorem [after Wooley, and Bourgain, Demeter and Guth]”, arXiv:1707.00119 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1404.3508](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.3508).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.00119

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Maximal valuation conjecture for sufficiently general valuations
record.statement: Let $\xi$ be a sufficiently general valuation parameter and let $t\ge 8+1/36$. Let $\operatorname{ord}_{\xi,t}$ denote the valuation written in the source, and let maximality mean that it attains the maximal value in the source's valuation-theoretic normalization. **Maximal valuation conjecture.** The valuation $\operatorname{ord}_{\xi,t}$ is maximal for every such $t$. The source states that this conjecture, proposed in Dumnicki–Harbourne–Küronya–Roé–Szemberg, implies Nagata's conjecture. Its general status is open.
record.source_name: Joaquim Roé and Paola Supino, “Nagata type statements”, arXiv:1707.00583 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.00583

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2017). “This statement holds true for $n$ a square, by Nagata's theorem, but it remains open for all other values of $n$.”

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for major index on two-row standard Young tableaux
record.statement:
Let $f_{(n-k,k),i}(q)$ be the generating polynomial for the major index of standard Young tableaux of shape $(n-k,k)$ having $i$ descents. Thus the relevant parameters are integers $n$, $k$, and $i$, in the range in which such tableaux exist.

**Two-row tableau unimodality conjecture.** For all $n$, $k$, and $i$, the polynomial $f_{(n-k,k),i}(q)$ is symmetric and unimodal, with central term $ni/2$.

The paper says this statement was empirically verified for $n\leq 30$ and that it would imply the major-index unimodality conjecture above through the displayed decomposition of $A_{n,i}(q)$. No proof of the statement is given, so it remains open in the source.
record.source_name: William J. Keith, “Major index over descent for pattern-avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1707.01200 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.01200

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

record.title: Pflueger's effective-weight conjecture for numerical semigroups
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a numerical semigroup of genus $g$, with gaps $l_1,\ldots,l_g$ and minimal generators $n_1,\ldots,n_e$. Define its **effective weight** by

$$
\operatorname{ewt}(S)=\sum_{i=1}^{g}\#\{j\mid n_j<l_i\}.
$$

**Pflueger's conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ewt}(S)\le\left\lfloor\frac{(g+1)^2}{8}\right\rfloor.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the relationship between numerical semigroups and Weierstrass semigroups of algebraic curves. It was formulated from computations for all semigroups of genus at most $50$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Nathan Kaplan, “Counting Numerical Semigroups”, arXiv:1707.02551 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02551

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2017). “In the final two sections of the paper, we discuss several refined counting questions and other open problems about numerical semigroups.”

record.title: Multiplicity estimate for singular loci of projective subschemes
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, and let $\delta\geqslant1$, $d\geqslant1$, and $s\geqslant0$ be integers. For a reduced pure-dimensional closed subscheme $X$ of $\mathbb P^n_K$ of dimension $d$ and degree $\delta$, whose singular locus has dimension $s$, let $S(X;B)$ be the set defined in the source. **Multiplicity estimate conjecture.** Uniformly for all such $X$, one should have

$$
\sum_{\xi\in S(X;B)}\mu_\xi(X)(\mu_\xi(X)-1)^{d-s}\ll_{n,K}\delta^{d-s+1}B^{s+1}.
$$

This is proposed in analogy with Liu's Conjecture 5.13 and concerns the dependence on the degree, height bound, and dimension of the singular locus in multiplicity-counting estimates.
record.source_name: Hao Wen and Chunhui Liu, “Counting Multiplicities in a Hypersurface over a Number Field”, arXiv:1707.07183 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.07183

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

record.title: Positivity conjecture for matrix counts of 123-avoiding permutations
record.statement: Let $w\in\mathfrak{S}_n$ be a $123$-avoiding permutation, meaning that it contains no subsequence order-isomorphic to $123$, and let $I_w$ be its diagram. Write $M_n(\overline{I_w},q)$ for the matrix count of rank-$n$ matrices over $\mathbf{F}_q$ supported in the complement of $I_w$. **Positivity conjecture.** For every $123$-avoiding permutation $w\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, $M_n(\overline{I_w},q)$ belongs to $\mathbb{N}[q]$. This strengthens the preceding conjecture for the particular permutation $v$; computations reported in the source support it for the tested cases, while the general statement remains open.

record.title: The conjecture that the quadratic supremum equals the sharp lower bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the energy function and let $M_2(\lambda,c_0)$ denote the corresponding supremum, with parameters $\lambda>0$ and $c_0>0$. **Quadratic-supremum conjecture.** For all $\lambda>0$ and $c_0>0$, 

$$
M_2(\lambda,c_0)=\sqrt{2}.
$$

The claim is motivated by numerical calculations showing that $M_2(\lambda,0)$ differs from $\sqrt{2}$ by approximately $2.7\times 10^{-9}$ for $\lambda\in[1,2]$, while the established bounds give $M_2(\lambda,0)\geq M_2(\lambda,c_0)\geq\sqrt{2}$.
record.source_name: Jonathan J. Bevan and Jonathan H. B. Deane, “A calibration method for estimating critical cavitation loads from below in 3D nonlinear elasticity”, arXiv:1707.08532 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.08532

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

record.title: The conjectured formula for the cubic supremum at large cutoff
record.statement:
Let $M_3(\lambda,c_0)$ be the cubic supremum, and let $c_1(\lambda)$ be a threshold such that $M_3(\lambda,c_0)=M_3(\lambda,c_1)$ for all $c_0\geq c_1(\lambda)$. For $\lambda\in[1,2]$, let $\nu_1\approx0.4501$, $\nu_2\approx1.764\times10^{-3}$, and $\nu_3\approx1.842$. **Large-cutoff cubic-supremum conjecture.** For all $c_0\geq c_1(\lambda)$ and $\lambda\in[1,2]$,

$$
M_3(\lambda,c_0)=M_3(\lambda,c_1)=\frac{\nu_1}{\lambda},
$$

where $c_1(\lambda)=\nu_3\lambda+\nu_2$. This conjecture records the numerical agreement observed for the threshold and the limiting supremum; the paper presents these values as numerical evidence rather than a proof.
record.source_name: Jonathan J. Bevan and Jonathan H. B. Deane, “A calibration method for estimating critical cavitation loads from below in 3D nonlinear elasticity”, arXiv:1707.08532 (2017).

record.title: Rolnick's character-range conjecture for independent Stanley sequences
record.statement: Let $S(A)=(a_n)$ be an independent Stanley sequence: there are constants $\lambda=\lambda(A)$ and $\kappa=\kappa(A)$ such that for all $k\ge\kappa$ and $0\le i<2^k$, $a_{2^k+i}=a_{2^k}+a_i$ and $a_{2^k}=2a_{2^k-1}-\lambda+1$. The constant $\lambda$ is called the character of $S(A)$. **Rolnick's character-range conjecture.** The range of the character function is exactly the set of nonnegative integers not in $\{1,3,5,9,11,15\}$. The conjecture concerns which characters occur among independent Stanley sequences; the source reports constructions for every character up to $75$ except the six listed values and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Richard Moy, Mehtaab Sawhney and David Stoner, “Characters of Independent Stanley Sequences”, arXiv:1708.01849 (2017).

record.title: Thomassé's two-acyclic-subgraphs conjecture for cycle reversions
record.statement: Let $D$ be a finite or infinite digraph, and let $\b1\mathcal{C}\in \mathbb{RS}(D)$ be a reversal sequence, with $D\hspace{-0.08\,\mathrm{cm}}\rcirclearrowright\mathcal{C}$ denoting the digraph obtained after the corresponding cycle reversals. **Thomassé's conjecture.** There is a $\b1\mathcal{C}\in \mathbb{RS}(D)$ such that $D\hspace{-0.08\,\mathrm{cm}}\rcirclearrowright\mathcal{C}$ is covered by two acyclic subgraphs. This conjecture is presented as a main motivation for the paper and concerns reducing the cyclic structure of an arbitrary digraph through cycle reversions; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

record.title: Conditional connectivity conjecture for transposition networks generated by connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G(\mathcal{T})$ be a connected graph, and let $G_n$ be the Cayley graph generated by $G(\mathcal{T})$. Write $\kappa^2(G_n)$ for its conditional connectivity parameter and $E(G(\mathcal{T}))$ for the edge set of $G(\mathcal{T})$. **Conditional connectivity conjecture.** If $G(\mathcal{T})$ contains a triangle, then

$$
\kappa^2(G_n)=4|E(G(\mathcal{T}))|-10
$$

for $n\geq 5$; if $G(\mathcal{T})$ contains no triangles, then

$$
\kappa^2(G_n)=4|E(G(\mathcal{T}))|-8
$$

for $n\geq 4$. The paper presents this as an open problem extending the determined cases for Cayley graphs generated by $k$-trees; general transposition networks generated by arbitrary sets of transpositions remain unresolved.
record.source_name: Weihua Yang, “A kind of conditional connectivity of transposition networks generated by k-trees”, arXiv:1708.02692 (2017).

record.title: Conjecture on flexible labelings of non-triangle-connected Laman graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a Laman graph. A graph is **triangle-connected** if any two edges can be joined by a sequence of edges in which consecutive edges lie in a common triangle. A **NAC-coloring** is an edge-coloring of $G$ with two colors such that every cycle is monochromatic or contains both colors, equivalently, no cycle has exactly one edge of one color. **Flexible-labeling conjecture.** If $G$ is not triangle-connected, then it has a NAC-coloring, and hence a flexible labeling. The conjecture gives a characterization of Laman graphs admitting flexible labelings; it was verified by computer for all Laman graphs with at most $12$ vertices, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Georg Grasegger, Jan Legerský and Josef Schicho, “Graphs with Flexible Labelings”, arXiv:1708.05298 (2018).

record.title: The multiplication-by-p conjecture for the Higgs-de Rham self-map
record.statement:
For $bbP^1_{W(\mathbb{F}_q)}$ with marked points $bb\{0,1,\infty,\lambda\}$, let $\pi:\mathcal{C}_\lambda\tobbP^1$ be the double cover ramified at these points. Let $[p]:\mathcal{C}_\lambda\to\mathcal{C}_\lambda$ denote multiplication by $p$, and let $\varphi_{\lambda,p}:bbP^1\tobbP^1$ be the self-map induced by the Higgs-de Rham flow.

**Multiplication-by-p conjecture.** The diagram commutes:

$$
\xymatrix{ \mathcal{C}_\lambda \ar[r]^{[p]} \ar[d]^{\pi} & \mathcal{C}_\lambda \ar[d]^{\pi} \\ bbP^1 \ar[r]^{\varphi_{\lambda,p}} & bbP^1 \\ }
$$

The conjecture identifies the Higgs-de Rham self-map with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on the associated elliptic curve. It was checked in the paper for all primes $p\leq 50$, but no general proof is given.
record.source_name: Ruiran Sun, Jinbang Yang and Kang Zuo, “Projective Crystalline Representations of Étale Fundamental Groups and Twisted Periodic Higgs-de Rham Flow”, arXiv:1709.01485 (2019).

record.title: The nonsquare supersingular lambda-invariant conjecture
record.statement: Assume $N$ is a prime with $N\equiv 1\pmod 4$, let $L$ be the set of supersingular lambda invariants in $\mathbf{F}_{N^2}$, and let $H'$ denote the derivative of the polynomial $H$ introduced in the supersingular lambda-invariant construction. **Nonsquare supersingular lambda-invariant conjecture.** For every $\lambda\in L$, $H'(\lambda)$ is not a square in $\mathbf{F}_{N^2}^{\times}$. The assertion was checked numerically for $N<2000$; it fails when $N\equiv3\pmod4$, so the stated case remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Emmanuel Lecouturier, “Higher Eisenstein elements, higher Eichler formulas and rank of Hecke algebras”, arXiv:1709.09114 (2018).

record.title: Manin–Mumford conjecture for curves in their Jacobians
record.statement: Let $C$ be an algebraic curve of genus $g \geq 2$, defined over a number field and embedded in its Jacobian $J$. **Manin–Mumford conjecture.** The set of torsion points of $J$ which lie in $C$ is finite. This conjecture was proved in 1983 by Raynaud, who generalized it to arbitrary subvarieties of an abelian variety; the corresponding general theorem describes the Zariski closure of the torsion points as a finite union of translates of abelian subvarieties by torsion points.
record.source_name: Aurélien Galateau and César Martínez, “A bound for the torsion on subvarieties of abelian varieties”, arXiv:1710.04577 (2017).

record.title: The -free graph sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}:=\mathcal{F}\setminus\{H_1,H_{26},H_{27}\}=\{H_2,\ldots,H_{25}\}$, where $\mathcal{F}$ is the family of $27$ forbidden induced subgraphs characterizing sum-perfect graphs. A graph is **$\mathcal{B}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{B}$. **The $\mathcal{B}$-free graph sum conjecture.** Every $\mathcal{B}$-free graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\alpha(G)+\omega(G)\geq |V(G)|-1.
$$

This was verified computationally for all graphs with at most $10$ vertices; the assertion remains open in general.
record.source_name: Bart Litjens, Sven Polak and Vaidy Sivaraman, “Sum-perfect graphs”, arXiv:1710.07546 (2017).

record.title: Acyclic matching bound for connected subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected subcubic graph, let $n(G)$ denote its number of vertices, and let $
u_{ac}(G)$ denote its acyclic matching number. **The acyclic matching conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that

$$
\nu_{ac}(G) \geq \frac{3n(G)}{11}-c
$$

for every connected subcubic graph $G$. The conjecture would be asymptotically best possible, as the paper describes a family of connected subcubic graphs $G_k$ satisfying $\nu_{ac}(G_k)=3n(G_k)/11$; its resolution is not indicated here.
record.source_name: M. Fürst and D. Rautenbach, “A lower bound on the acyclic matching number of subcubic graphs”, arXiv:1710.10076 (2017).

record.title: Lando's congruence for the universal $sl_2$ weight system
record.statement:
For each $ngeq 1$, let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the $n$-chord diagram in which every chord intersects every other chord, and let $D_n=varphi(\mathcal{D}_n)inmathbb{Z}[x]$. Write $(h_n)_{ngeq 0}=(1,1,2,7,38,295,ldots)$ for the normalized median Genocchi numbers. **Lando's conjecture.** For all $ngeq 1$,

$$
D_nequiv (-1)^{n-1}h_{n-1}xmod x^2.
$$

The paper proves this particular case later as a consequence of its master theorem, so the original conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Ange Bigeni, “A generalization of the Kreweras triangle through the universal sl_2 weight system”, arXiv:1712.05475 (2018).

record.title: The natural deficiency conjecture for convex drawings of complete graphs
record.statement:
For a drawing $D$ of $K_n$, define its **deficiency** by

$$
\delta(D)=\operatorname{cr}(D)-H(n).
$$

The drawing $D$ has the **natural deficiency property** if, for every vertex $v$ of $K_n$,

$$
\delta(D-v)\leq 2\delta(D).
$$

Here a convex drawing is a drawing in which all vertices lie on the boundary of the unbounded face. **The natural deficiency conjecture.** For every $k\geq 2$, every convex drawing of $K_{2k}$ has the natural deficiency property. This is presented as a weakening of the Hill Conjecture and arose in connection with lower bounds for the crossing number of $K_{13}$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Alan Arroyo, Dan McQuillan, R. Bruce Richter and Gelasio Salazar, “Convex drawings of the complete graph: topology meets geometry”, arXiv:1712.06380 (2017).

record.title: Degree-three generic list recovery for MRA with projection
record.statement: Let $p\geq 3$ be odd, let $V=\mathbb{R}^p$ with the cyclic-shift action of $G=\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and let the projection identify opposite entries as in MRA with projection. **MRA-with-projection conjecture.** For every odd $p\geq 3$, generic list recovery is possible at degree $3$. This is supported by Jacobian-criterion computations through $p=21$; degree $2$ cannot suffice because projection loses information.
record.source_name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Ben Blum-Smith, Joe Kileel, Amelia Perry, Jonathan Niles-Weed and Alexander S. Wein, “Estimation under group actions: recovering orbits from invariants”, arXiv:1712.10163 (2023).

record.title: Degree-three recovery thresholds for heterogeneous MRA
record.statement:
Let $K\geq 2$ and let $p$ be the signal dimension in heterogeneous MRA. Define

$$
\mathcal{U}=p+2+\left\lfloor\frac p2\right\rfloor+\left\lceil\frac{(p-1)(p-2)}6\right\rceil.
$$

**Heterogeneous MRA recovery conjecture.** Generic unique recovery is possible at degree $3$ if $\mathcal{U}>Kp+K-1$, while generic list recovery is possible at degree $3$ precisely if $\mathcal{U}\geq Kp+K-1$. Equivalently, the latter requires $p\geq1$ for $K=2$, $p\geq12$ for $K=3$, $p\geq18$ for $K=4$, and $p\geq6K-5$ for every $K\geq5$. The conjecture was rigorously verified by exact-arithmetic Jacobian and Hessian tests up to $K=15$ and the corresponding critical values of $p$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Ben Blum-Smith, Joe Kileel, Amelia Perry, Jonathan Niles-Weed and Alexander S. Wein, “Estimation under group actions: recovering orbits from invariants”, arXiv:1712.10163 (2023).

record.title: The range conjecture for the Dedekind-sum auxiliary function $\lambda$
record.statement:
For an integer $q\geq 2$, let $\Lambda_q$ be the set of residue classes produced by the auxiliary function $\lambda(a,t,t^{*})$, and define

$$
\Gamma_q=\begin{cases}\\{24s:s\in\mathbb Z/(q^2-1)\mathbb Z\\}&q\text{ is a square},\\\\\\{12s:s\in\mathbb Z/(q^2-1)\mathbb Z\\}&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$
 **The range conjecture.** For every integer $q\geq 2$, $\Lambda_q=\Gamma_q$. This conjecture specifies the full range of the auxiliary residue-valued function and would imply Girstmair's numerator restriction conjecture. It is open in general, although the paper proves the corresponding assertions computationally for $2\leq q\leq 200$ and in several infinite families.
record.source_name: Michael Kural, “Dedekind Sums with Even Denominators”, arXiv:1801.00517 (2018).

record.title: Rank-ordering conjecture for overpartition ranks modulo 6
record.statement:
Let $\overline{N}(m,6,n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ whose rank is congruent to $m$ modulo $6$. For $n\geq 11$, the rank counts satisfy the following orderings according to $n$ modulo $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline{N}(0,6,3n)&\geq\overline{N}(1,6,3n)=\overline{N}(3,6,3n)\geq\overline{N}(2,6,3n),\\
\overline{N}(0,6,3n+1)&\geq\overline{N}(1,6,3n+1)=\overline{N}(3,6,3n+1)\geq\overline{N}(2,6,3n+1),\\
\overline{N}(1,6,3n+2)&\geq\overline{N}(2,6,3n+2)\geq\overline{N}(0,6,3n+2)\geq\overline{N}(3,6,3n+2).
\end{aligned}
$$

**Rank-ordering conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 11$, these inequalities and equalities hold.
record.source_name: Bin Wei and Helen W. J. Zhang, “Generalized Lambert Series Identities and Applications in Rank Differences”, arXiv:1801.04643 (2018).
record.references:

record.title: Prime correlation conjecture for Kloosterman sums and cusp-form eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $f$ be a fixed primitive cusp form, holomorphic or Maass, and let $\lambda_f(p)$ denote its Hecke eigenvalue at a prime $p$. Write $\mathcal{L}=\log X$. **Prime correlation conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $X$,

$$
\sum_{p\leq X}\lambda_f(p)\mathrm{Kl}(1,p)=o\left(X\mathcal{L}^{-1}\right).
$$

The conjecture is proposed as a correlation estimate between Kloosterman sums and Hecke eigenvalues. If true, the source says it would imply that for $100\%$ of primes $p$, one has $\lambda_f(p)\neq\mathrm{Kl}(1,p)$ for each primitive cusp form $f$, giving a negative answer to Katz's modularity problem III. No resolution is given.
record.source_name: Ping Xi, “When Kloosterman sums meet Hecke eigenvalues”, arXiv:1801.07658 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07658

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Integer correlation conjecture for Kloosterman sums and cusp-form eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $f$ be a fixed primitive cusp form, holomorphic or Maass, and let $\lambda_f(n)$ denote its Hecke eigenvalue at $n$. Write $\mathcal{L}=\log X$. **Integer correlation conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $X$,

$$
\sum_{n\leq X}\lambda_f(n)\mathrm{Kl}(1,n)=O\left(X\mathcal{L}^{-2018}\right).
$$

This is a conjectured power-logarithmic saving for the correlation over consecutive integers. The source gives no evidence of a proof or disproof, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Ping Xi, “When Kloosterman sums meet Hecke eigenvalues”, arXiv:1801.07658 (2019).

record.title: Singular ramified irregular vertex operator conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p,q$ be positive integers, let

$$
c=13-6\left(t+\frac{1}{t}\right),\qquad \Delta_{p,q}=\frac{(pt-q)^2-(t-1)^2}{4t},
$$

and let $\chi_{p,q}$ be the singular vector of level $pq$ in $M_{\Delta_{p,q}}$. A ramified irregular vertex operator is called singular when it annihilates this vector. **Singular ramified vertex-operator conjecture.** For every positive integers $p,q$, a singular ramified irregular vertex operator $\Phi^{\Delta_{p,q}}_{\Lambda,\Lambda}(\alpha,\beta,c_{\emptyset};z)$ exists; its parameters $\alpha$, $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{2r-1}$ and $c_{\emptyset}^{(m)}$ are polynomials in $c$, $\Lambda_r,\ldots,\Lambda_{2r-1}$ and $\Lambda_{2r-1}^{-1}$, and there are $pq$ such parameter sets counted with multiplicity. The source does not report a proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Hajime Nagoya, “Remarks on irregular conformal blocks and Painlevé III and II tau functions”, arXiv:1804.04782 (2018).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04782

record.title: Zauner's weak conjecture on symmetric informationally complete measurements
record.statement:
For each positive integer $d\geq 2$, a **SIC POVM** is a set of $d^2$ rank-one positive operators on $\mathbb{C}^d$ that forms an informationally complete symmetric positive operator-valued measure; equivalently, unit vectors $w_i\in\mathbb{C}^d$ generate a SIC POVM when $|\langle w_i,w_j\rangle|^2=\frac{1}{d+1}$ for all $i\ne j$. **Zauner's weak conjecture.** For every positive integer $d\geq 2$, there exist $d^2$ unit vectors $\{w_i\}_{i=1}^{d^2}\subseteq\mathbb{C}^d$ such that

$$
|\langle w_i,w_j\rangle|^2=\frac{1}{d+1}
$$

for all $i\ne j$. This is the SIC POVM existence problem. It remains open in general, although concrete solutions are known in many dimensions, including $d=1$ through $21$, $24$, $28$, $30$, $31$, and $35$.
record.source_name: Satish K. Pandey, Vern I. Paulsen, Jitendra Prakash and Mizanur Rahaman, “Entanglement Breaking Rank and the existence of SIC POVMs”, arXiv:1805.04583 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04583

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2018). “The existence of a SIC POVM for each dimension $d\geq 2$ is still an open problem, however in some specific dimensions $(d=1-21,24, 28, 30, 31, 35 \ \text{etc.})$ concrete solutions of SIC sets have been found.”

record.title: Irreducibility conjecture for the non-cyclotomic factor of $f_k$
record.statement:
Let

$$
f_k=1-x+x^k-x^{2k-1}+x^{2k}
$$

be the polynomial considered above, and let $\Phi_n$ denote the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial. Write $(f_k,\Phi_6\Phi_{10}\Phi_{12})$ for the greatest common divisor of $f_k$ and $\Phi_6\Phi_{10}\Phi_{12}$. **Irreducibility conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 1$, the polynomial

$$
\frac{f_k}{(f_k,\Phi_6\Phi_{10}\Phi_{12})}
$$

is irreducible over the rationals and non-cyclotomic. The conjecture extends the computational verification for $5\leq k\leq 1000$; establishing irreducibility and non-cyclotomicity for all $k$ remains open.
record.source_name: Andrés Herrera-Poyatos and Pieter Moree, “Coefficients and higher order derivatives of cyclotomic polynomials: old and new”, arXiv:1805.05207 (2018).

record.title: Existence of constant-curvature ball packings under bounded vertex-degree variation
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a triangulation with vertex set $V$, and let $d_i$ denote the vertex degree at $i\in V$. A **real ball packing** is an element of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{T}}$, while a **virtual ball packing** is an element of $\mathds{R}_{>0}^N\setminus\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{T}}$. A ball packing may therefore be real or virtual.

**Constant-curvature packing conjecture.** If

$$
|d_i-d_j|\leq 10
$$

for every $i,j\in V$, then there exists a real or virtual ball packing with constant curvature.

This conjecture proposes an existence criterion for constant-curvature packings without requiring the triangulation to be regular. The source gives no resolution or further evidence beyond the preceding convergence results, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Huabin Ge, Wenshuai Jiang and Liangming Shen, “On the deformation of ball packings”, arXiv:1805.10573 (2018).

record.title: The dimension-seven conjecture for tritangents of space sextics
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth space sextic contained in a singular quadric. Let $\alpha=\theta-\theta_0\in \mathrm{J}(C)[2]\backslash\{0\}$, where $\theta$ is one of the $120$ odd theta characteristics and $\theta_0$ is the vanishing even theta characteristic. The space $W_{C,\alpha}$ is the associated space appearing in the tritangent construction.

**Dimension-seven conjecture.**

$$
\dim W_{C,\alpha}=7.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the paper's computation showing this dimension for an example and by the observation that it occurs for every $\alpha$ arising from one of the $120$ odd theta characteristics in that example. Its general validity for smooth space sextics contained in singular quadrics is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Turku Ozlum Celik, Avinash Kulkarni, Yue Ren and Mahsa Sayyary Namin, “Tritangents and Their Space Sextics”, arXiv:1805.11702 (2018).

record.title: The $d$-sequence conjecture for coefficients of uniform-matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
record.statement:
For integers $m$ and $d$, and $0\leq i\leq d$, define

$$
f_m(d,i)=\sum_{h=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{(m-h)\binom{m}{h}}\binom{i+m}{m-h-1}\binom{i-1+h}{h}\binom{d-i+h}{h}.
$$

A finite sequence of real numbers is an $n$-sequence when the associated polynomial has real zeros of one common sign. **The $d$-sequence conjecture.** The sequence $\{f_m(d,i)\}_{i=0}^{d}$ is a $d$-sequence for every $m$ and $d$. Numerical evidence supports the conjecture, and the paper verifies the needed cases $2\leq m\leq 15$ to establish real-rootedness there; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Alice L. L. Gao, Linyuan Lu, Matthew H. Y. Xie, Arthur L. B. Yang and Philip B. Zhang, “The Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of uniform matroids”, arXiv:1806.10852 (2018).

record.title: Xiao-Song Lin's conjecture relating the colored Jones polynomial to $L^2$-Alexander torsion
record.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a knot. For every $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $J_K(N,x)\in\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}]$ be the normalized $N$-th colored Jones polynomial. For $t\in\mathbb{C}^*$, let $\tau^{(2)}(K)(t)$ denote the $L^2$-Alexander torsion of $K$. **Xiao-Song Lin's conjecture.** For every $t\in\mathbb{C}^*$,

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\left|J_K\left(N,\exp\left(\frac{2\pi i t}{N}\right)\right)\right|^{\frac{1}{3N}}\mathrel{\dot{=}}\tau^{(2)}(K)(t)\cdot\max\{1,|t|\}.
$$

Here $\mathrel{\dot{=}}$ is the equality notation used in the source. The conjecture was formulated by Xiao-Song Lin in 2005, and the source notes that its final form is subject to modification; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Fathi Ben Aribi, Stefan Friedl and Gerrit Herrmann, “The leading coefficient of the L^2-Alexander torsion”, arXiv:1806.10965 (2021).
